predecessors.note: The rebel zone is cut out of Cliopatria's Republic of Cuba: Cuba has 12 cells less in 1958 (498 against 510) and keeps them out in 1959.

land.text: the Sierra Maestra, where 'the mountains came under Castro's control' (3,144 km2 in Granma and Santiago de Cuba on Cliopatria's grid)

successors.note: The rebels do not part with the zone: they take the state. Batista 'fled Cuba by air for the Dominican Republic just hours later on 1 January 1959' and Castro 'arrived in Havana on 8 January'. Cliopatria returns the zone to Cuba only in 1960, as 'Communist Cuba'.

correction.text: shape unchanged, but it holds for 1958 only: from 1 January 1959 the rebels are the government and the Sierra Maestra is part of Cuba, not a separate zone

keyframe_review.note: The year 1959 is wrong: Cliopatria keeps the zone apart through 1959 and gives it to 'Communist Cuba' in 1960, but the page has the dictator gone and the rebels in Havana in the first days of January 1959. The extent is unverified: the page gives no area, only 'Ultimately, the mountains came under Castro's control'; 3,144 km2 (12 cells, 19.9-20.2 N, 77.0-75.8 W) is plausible for a mountain base. A rebel zone has no infobox area to compare. The label 'Cuban Communists' is Cliopatria's: the page has the communists (Popular Socialist Party) as one partner in a coalition whose influence waned 'in favor of the 26th of July Movement', so the zone is Castro's 26 July Movement's.

region.text: the Sierra Maestra, where 'the mountains came under Castro's control' (3,144 km2 in Granma and Santiago de Cuba on Cliopatria's grid)

ledger.note: 1958: the rebels hold the Sierra Maestra. After the Granma landing 'on 2 December' (1956, Playa Las Coloradas, Niquero) 'the band of rebels began to make their way into the Sierra Maestra mountains'; Radio Rebelde was 'set up in February 1958'. The page dates neither the base nor its extent ('Ultimately, the mountains came under Castro's control'), so the year is Cliopatria's; the page has the rebels entering the mountains after the landing, with no date for that.

region.text: the Sierra Maestra, where 'the mountains came under Castro's control' (3,144 km2 in Granma and Santiago de Cuba on Cliopatria's grid)

ledger.note: July 1958: Batista's summer offensive reaches the heart of the Sierra Maestra. 'The battle [of El Jigüe] spanned from 11 to 21 July 1958 and is widely considered to be a "turning point" in the revolution.' The page does not date the offensive's start (Operation Verano); the first dated battle is used.

region.text: the Sierra Maestra, where 'the mountains came under Castro's control' (3,144 km2 in Granma and Santiago de Cuba on Cliopatria's grid)

ledger.note: 8 August 1958: the offensive fails. 'The Battle of Las Mercedes (29 July–8 August 1958) was the last battle of Operation Verano' and 'By 8 August, Castro's entire army had escaped back into the mountains.' The rebels keep the zone.

ledger.note: December 1958: the rebel columns attack Santa Clara. 'Three columns were sent against Santa Clara under the command of Che Guevara, Jaime Vega, and Camilo Cienfuegos'; the page dates the offensive to December. The 50 km radius is the reading from the city name.

ledger.note: 31 December 1958: the Battle of Santa Clara. 'On 31 December 1958, the Battle of Santa Clara took place in a scene of great confusion'; Batista fled the next day. The page excerpt read does not state who held the city when the shooting stopped.

sources.title: Cuban Revolution
sources.note: The Granma landing, the Sierra Maestra, Radio Rebelde, Operation Verano and its battles, Santa Clara, Batista's flight on 1 January 1959, Havana on 8 January. Silent on the zone's extent, on the Second Front's date and on the invasion of the west.

sources.title: Communist Party of Cuba
sources.note: Cliopatria's own link: the present party was founded 3 October 1965; the Popular Socialist Party (communists), the 26th of July Movement and the Revolutionary Directory merged into the ORI in July 1961. Silent on the party's role in the fighting and on any territory held: the label 'Cuban Communists' is not supported.

notes: BUDGET: two pages (Cuban Revolution; Communist Party of Cuba). LABEL: Cliopatria's 'Cuban Communists' (wiki title 'Communist Party of Cuba') is the Sierra Maestra zone of Castro's 26th of July Movement; the Communist Party of Cuba page dates the present party to 3 October 1965 and the ORI merger to July 1961 and says nothing of the party holding land, while the Cuban Revolution page names the Popular Socialist Party only as one partner of a coalition. The display name follows the page, the Cliopatria name stays in cliopatria_names and alt_names. YEARS: the zone is rebel 1958 only on the pages (the rebels take the state on 1 January 1959); Cliopatria's 1959 year and its return of the zone to Cuba only in 1960 ('Communist Cuba') should be corrected in the republic-of-cuba and communist-cuba dossiers (the republic-of-cuba dossier already records a 1 January 1959 gain). EXTENT UNVERIFIED: the pages give no area. The Granma landing was on 2 December 1956 and the rebels then made their way into the Sierra Maestra (no date for that), while Cliopatria draws the zone only for 1958; no earlier keyframe was possible. COMPILING: the two contest events are ten weeks and two weeks long, with months; a one-year step should not hide the rebel colour for all of 1958. NOT OPENED (budget): 26th of July Movement, Operation Verano, Battle of Santa Clara, Second Front. Gazetteer: the region 'Sierra Maestra' (mountain range in Granma and Santiago de Cuba, about 77.0-76.0 W, 19.9-20.2 N) is not in regions.jsonl; the Cliopatria shape stands in for it. Rulers omitted; capitals empty (no seat on the pages).
